answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying reputation to a slowly earned stake: each agent deposits funds that vest over time, like an ember that must be tended before it gives light. Newcomers start on the knoll, visible but untrusted, and only gain full trading rights after a history of honest, verified work. An attacker creating thousands of fake agents faces a steep bill: every identity needs its own deposit and waiting period, while the ivory tower of instant trust never exists. Cost scales with the attack, not the defence.
